title: Hybrid prefill-decode scheduler with adaptive routing and acceptance metrics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a hybrid prefill/decode scheduling layer that enables speculative decoding across a fast low-cost candidate model and a higher-quality primary model. The scheduler should: (1) route early decode tokens to a cheap model to reduce perceived latency for interactive workloads; (2) monitor acceptance metrics and decide when to promote speculative tokens vs. fallback to the primary model; (3) preserve correctness and support safe KV-cache merges or rollbacks; (4) provide observability hooks for acceptance rate, cost delta, and end-to-end latency. This ticket covers runtime changes (scheduling, routing policy), kernel/attention compatibility checks, telemetry, and a safe rollout path with canary and automatic fallback policy. It does not include UI work for the Console (separate PM ticket).

acceptance_criteria: Scheduler passes integration tests for IDLE->PREFILL->SPECULATE->EVALUATE->COMMIT/REPLAY transitions
Telemetry emits per-request acceptance_score, acceptance_decision, fallback_reason, and cost_delta (sampled at 100%)
Canary run at 1% traffic for 72h with acceptance_rate >= 90% and no customer-facing regressions (synthetic smoke tests green)
Fallback path (replay on primary) must not increase 99th percentile latency by more than 2x vs baseline primary-only decode for canary traffic
No silent data corruption: KV caches after COMMIT must match an authoritative primary-only run for identical prompts within a tolerance for quantization differences
decisions: Use a separate speculative KV namespace to avoid in-place evictions on the primary cache during canary and early rollout

Acceptance metric will be a composite score: token-level logit-distance + prefix-likelihood ratio + alignment with trigger heuristics (length, temperature) — thresholds will be dynamically tunable via ConfigService
Initial candidate models: 4-bit quantized Llama-family 3B for latency, with a fallback to standard primary (customer-selected) models — later expand to distilled decoder-only families
Do not perform optimistic in-place KV merge for rollout phase. Use 'replay-on-primary' rollback to guarantee correctness until kernel-level merge safely validated
Routing policy is adaptive: prefer local candidate pools for sub-50ms tail latencies; fall back to regional primary on resource pressure
